comparison: Both evaluate growth measurement methodology and temporal dynamics (C25-C28). OpenEval focuses on these specific claims, while peer review groups them with volumetric claims (C29-C31) and praises the novel measurement approach broadly.

OpenEval evaluates volumetric measurements (C29-C31) separately, while peer review combines these with temporal growth claims (C25-C28) in a single evaluation praising the comprehensive growth measurement approach.

Both address allometric growth patterns (C42-C43). OpenEval includes additional claims (C44-C45) about biphasic patterns and multiple control mechanisms. Peer review also includes mutant allometric data (C92-C93) in the same evaluation.
OpenEval evaluates altered allometric relationships in mutants (C92-C94) separately. Peer review groups these with wild-type allometric growth (C42-C43) as part of the comprehensive analysis.

Both evaluate Ds gradient scaling along AP axis (C50-C55). OpenEval focuses on these specific gradient characterization claims. Peer review also includes volume-scaling claims (C71, C81) in recognizing gradient scaling as a novel result.

Both evaluate volume-scaling experiments with trol(RNAi) (C73-C77). OpenEval and peer review both support these findings. Peer review also includes the complementary cell number manipulation (C78-C83) in the same evaluation.

Both evaluate cell number manipulation experiments (C78-C83). OpenEval treats this separately from trol(RNAi), while peer review groups both volume-scaling experiments together as supporting gradient scaling to tissue size.

Both evaluate Fat gradient characterization (C56-C60). OpenEval focuses on gradient properties and dynamics. Peer review also includes post-transcriptional regulation claims (C61-C63) and summary statement (C177) in recognizing the Fat gradient as a novel discovery.
OpenEval evaluates post-transcriptional regulation of Fat (C61-C63) separately. Peer review groups this with Fat gradient characterization (C56-C60) as part of the novel Fat gradient discovery.

Both evaluate fat mutant phenotypes (C84-C87). OpenEval treats fat and ds mutants separately. Peer review groups both mutant phenotypes (C84-C91) together as consistent with known Hippo pathway roles.
Both evaluate ds mutant phenotypes (C88-C91). OpenEval emphasizes distinct mechanisms from fat mutants. Peer review groups with fat mutant data (C84-C87) as part of comprehensive mutant analysis.

Both evaluate wing-specific Ds knockdown and allometric effects (C99-C102). OpenEval focuses on these specific claims. Peer review also includes autonomous requirement claims (C106-C109) in acknowledging localized manipulation experiments.

Both evaluate autonomous growth control by Fat/Ds (C106-C109). OpenEval includes additional claims (C103-C105) about Fat knockdown. Peer review groups with allometric scaling claims (C99-C102) as part of localized manipulation experiments.

Both evaluate altered cell cycle scaling in ds(RNAi) (C127-C129). OpenEval treats this separately from wild-type. Peer review groups with wild-type cell cycle data (C3-C4, C125-C126, C130) as part of the comprehensive cell cycle analysis.
OpenEval evaluates fat(RNAi) cell cycle scaling (C130) separately. Peer review groups this with all cell cycle scaling data (C3-C4, C125-C129) in recognizing the key finding about cell cycle control.

Both evaluate the conclusion that Fat/Ds tune cell cycle coupling (C134-C136). OpenEval treats this as summary inference. Peer review groups with model predictions (C131-C133) in accepting cell cycle control as primary mechanism.

Both evaluate Ds overexpression experiments showing normal growth despite altered gradients (C137-C141). OpenEval and peer review both support this as challenging the gradient model. Peer review also includes Ds amplification data (C142-C147).

Both evaluate Ds amplification experiments (C142-C147). OpenEval treats this separately from Ds overexpression. Peer review groups both Ds manipulation experiments (C137-C147) together in recognizing the challenge to gradient models.

Both evaluate Fat manipulation experiments showing normal growth (C148-C152). Perfect agreement that this challenges the gradient model. Both recognize this as a critical result demonstrating gradients are not necessary for growth regulation.

Both evaluate the negative result that Fj does not regulate Fat gradient (C64-C66). Perfect agreement on claims. OpenEval emphasizes importance for ruling out mechanisms, peer review accepts as part of comprehensive gradient characterization.

Both evaluate Fat gradient changes in ds mutants (C67-C70). High overlap with OpenEval including C70 (consistency with previous work) that peer review groups with summary statement C178 about Fat gradient dependence on Ds.

Both evaluate cellular mechanism of Ds growth control (C119-C121). Perfect agreement that Ds regulates cell number rather than cell size. Both accept this as establishing the cellular basis of growth regulation.
